OWN represents managerial ownership and is either set equal to RCEOOWN (model 1)

CEO ownership, CEOOWN, is defined as the number of shares held by the CEO divided by the total number of shares outstanding. Ownership by the top five managers, TOP5, is defined analogously.
In our primary tests, we measure both CEO and top 5 manager ownership excluding shares granted in options.

research_interest_evidence.quote: H1: Accounting conservatism is negatively related to managerial ownership.

Concentrating first on model 1, we find that the coefficient on RET ∗ OWN is significantly positive, while the coefficient on RET ∗ NEG ∗ OWN is significantly negative. These results suggest that, as managerial ownership declines, earnings become less timely in recognizing good news and more asymmetrically timely in recognizing bad news.

review_notes: Source-first scope: retain the primary H1 relationship in section 4.1 / Table 2, which the authors call their primary results. CEO direct ownership and top-five-manager direct ownership are the two stated primary ownership proxies; each is estimated with the same complete Basu interaction model and controls.

Exclude the later H2 IOS-residualization models (Table 4 ownership prediction and Table 5 conservatism regression) because they test the distinct after-controlling-for-IOS hypothesis and use a subsequent decomposition. The Table 3 options test, director/founder analyses, and three-year Basu measure are follow-up designs. Table 4 is not a dependency of the retained Table 2 models.

The paper identifies annual cross-sectional Fama–MacBeth estimation and Newey–West corrected time-series inference, but does not name the estimator used within each annual cross section. Table 2 reports an average N over 11 fits, not an exact per-fit N.

The SIC 7370 classification for LIT is conflicting: the Table 2 note lists 7370, while descriptive text on physical page 15 lists 7370–7374. Both statements are preserved; the actual coding remains unresolved.
results_review_notes: Table 2 is the selected baseline family. Later specifications in other tables are outside scope.
The coefficient estimates are means across 11 annual regressions, and the t-statistics test those means using Newey–West corrected time-series standard errors. Degrees of freedom are not stated.
Table 1 Panel B reports no per-variable N; the Table 1 Panel A total sample is not used to populate N statistics for each descriptive row.
The LIT SIC coding differs between the Table 1 note and descriptive prose; this source discrepancy is preserved as a review note and the frozen Table 2 coding is unchanged.
